name: Graphic Arts
tagline: Got an idea? Let’s turn it into something people can see, share, and remember!
description:
In Graphic Arts, students learn how to think like designers and create like professionals. From bold logos and eye-catching advertisements to magazine layouts, T-shirts, packaging, and digital graphics, students use Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign to bring their ideas to life.

Along the way, students explore color, composition, typography, branding, and visual communication while building a portfolio of real-world design projects. Whether you’re already a creative pro or just discovering your design skills, there’s always something new to create!

courses.title: Intro to Graphic Design
courses.desc:
Students explore the fundamentals of graphic design through hands-on projects that introduce color, typography, composition, branding, layout, and visual communication.

Using industry-standard Adobe software, students learn the basics of Illustrator, and Photoshop while creating everything from logos and advertisements to digital graphics and print projects.

No previous design experience is needed — just curiosity, creativity, and a willingness to try new things! This course gives students the foundation they need to continue through the Graphic Design and Graphic Communication pathways while discovering how creative ideas can become real-world designs.

courses.title: Graphics Design and Production
courses.desc:
In Graphic Design & Production, students build on the skills they learned in Intro and begin working more like professional graphic designers. Students tackle larger, more challenging projects while developing their skills in Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign.

From creating logos and brand identities to posters, publications, packaging, T-shirts, and other print and digital projects, students learn how to take a design from an initial idea all the way to a finished product.

Students also get hands-on experience with print production and the graphic arts process, learning how designs are prepared, produced, and turned into something you can actually hold, wear, and share.

More creativity. More projects. More real-world design experience. This is where students start building a portfolio that shows what they can really do!

courses.title: Graphic Design II — Advanced
courses.desc: Advanced projects, branding, and portfolio development.
